item.title: Estate Sale of Mary Wood — Fri Nov 20, 10:00 AM — NJ
item.description:
For nearly six decades, this New Jersey couple had a front-row seat to the world of fine things. She ran estate sales across the state for more than 40 years, and in his retirement years he ran an art gallery. Their trained eyes and lifelong love of beautiful, well-made objects are reflected throughout their home: museum-quality paintings, Oriental and Native American rugs, period furniture, fine jewelry and crystal, alongside the playful finds of true collectors, including antique trains, vintage toys, a pool table, and a workshop full of old tools. item.description: An immersive evening of breath, connection, and renewal. For one special evening, Loopwell transforms into an intimate, candlelit sanctuary for a guided breathwork experience with Julie and Billy of Spirit 11ouse. Surrounded by soft candlelight, lush greenery, and a calming atmosphere, you’ll be invited to slow down, turn inward, and reconnect with yourself through the power of breath. item.title: Simple Sitting Meditation (15 minutes) — Wed Dec 2, 11:00 AM
item.description:
The Mindful Stream In these sessions, I will be doing guided meditations where we simply sit and notice what arises.
There is no agenda and no plan for how these sessions unfold. I might start off simply by asking us to notice what is already present. By becoming aware of what’s going on in our heads and in our body.
Then, the meditation may take on a life of its own.
Our job is to simply be present to what arises. We may notice the mind moving and chattering about. Or we may notice that it’s completely silent.
The goal here, if there is one, is to simply let ourselves be as we are.
Source: Meetup: The Mindful Stream

item.title: Book Talk: 20 Over 60 by Beth Weinhouse and David Galef — Thu Dec 3, 6:00 PM — Montclair Main - Conference Room
item.description:
In their new anthology 20 OVER 60 (Regal House; October 6, 2026), editors Beth Weinhouse and David Galef—also co-editors of the anthology 20 OVER 40—present a portrait of later life that is consistently overlooked, in a culture obsessed with youth. The twenty short stories—including ones by Joyce Carol Oates, Paul Theroux, and Jane Gardam—are vibrant, moving, and often hilarious, capturing the texture of life after sixty in all its complexity.
Among the characters readers will meet: a retired couple whose hobby is stealing pepper mills from high-end restaurants, a woman juggling her husband and ex-husband staying in the same hospital, a futuristic nursing home whose designers become its unhappy residents, an older woman trying her hand at online dating, and a grandfather helping his granddaughter scatter her mother's ashes. item.title: Your Library, Your Voice: Help Shape the New Library! — Mon Dec 7, 11:00 AM — Montclair Main - Tower Room
item.description:
What does the library mean to you? As we prepare for our upcoming renovation, we want to build a space that truly serves our community—and that starts with listening to you.
Join us for an open feedback session to share whatever is on your mind:
How you use the library today
What you love about our programs, collections, and spaces
Frustrations or obstacles you've run into
What you’d love to see in the renovated space
Whether you have big design ideas or just want to tell us about your favorite books, we're all ears. Your feedback will directly guide the design, programs, and future of our library.

Gina Chung Fortt has 14 years of experience in the Elementary grades as a classroom teacher and pull-out Reading Specialist. Gina is super passionate about supporting struggling readers and empowering parents and caregivers to guide their child(ren)'s literacy journey.
Please sign up for a 30-minute consultation with our Youth Services Reading Specialist. Some topics may include:
How to support your child's reading at home Review your child's current reading assessment (please bring copies, if possible) Learn what resources we have at the library to check out for your developing or struggling reader Other areas of concern or curiosity regarding your child's literacy development
Sign up HERE for a slot!
Adults only. Registration is required.

item.title: Open Book, Open Mind; Hernan Diaz, "Ply" — Mon Dec 7, 6:30 PM — Montclair Main - Auditorium
item.description:
Pulitzer Prize-winning writer Hernan Diaz ("Trust") will talk about his much anticipated new novel, "Ply."
“'Ply' is majestic. A cracked mirror world, a lot like ours; peopled by survivors, a lot like us; sentences so fine they break the skin; a plot that swerves through loss, love, trust, betrayal, art, science, society and control.” —David Mitchell ("Cloud Atlas")
Doors open at 6 p.m. The discussion will be followed by an audience Q&A and book sales and signing with Watchung Booksellers.
Open Book / Open Mind is sponsored by Montclair Public Library Foundation, Watchung Booksellers, Anonymous, David and Mary Lee Jones, and our individual Underwriters. We are also grateful for the generous support of our in-kind sponsors, First Congregational Church of Montclair, The George, and Amanti Vino. To support Open Book / Open Mind and other library programs, click here to donate.
Source: Libcal Bccls 10306

item.title: Island Beach State Park — Sat Nov 21, 8:45 AM — NJ
item.description:
One of the gems of the state park system, Island Beach has miles of beach, tidal wetlands, maritime forest and thickets that can host a good diversity of birds, especially if the winds are right. November sees peak numbers of migratory waterfowl, loons, gannets, and other seabirds and is a good time of year for rarities. There is a $5 entry fee for NJ residents who do not have a state park pass or are 65 years of age or older. Be prepared for several hours of walking on flat terrain, sometimes sandy. Bring lunch. Led by Scott Barnes and Linda Mack. A NOTE ON MEETING LOCATION! We’ll meet just outside of the park entrance, in the median parking lot at the end of Rt. 35. PRE-REGISTRATION REQUIRED COST: $25 Members, $30 Non-members REGISTER HERE
Source: NJ Audubon

item.title: Chester County Horse-Shoe and More Hike — Sun Nov 29, 8:30 AM
item.description: Metrotrails: NJ, PA, NY Metropolitan Area Hiking and More! Join us for this point to point hike in rural Chester County Pennsylvania, featuring some prominent trails including the Horse-Shoe Trail, as well as other connections! I have planned this one specifically because it is a Sunday that hunting isn't permitted in some of the preserves along the way, and because most of the route is pleasant but within safety zones. After meeting at Bryn Coed, we will shuttle with as few vehicles as possible to our start point, at Highland Farm Park. We'll start by walking some of the trails to the north, through fields and a wood line, out into a development. We'll cut through the development and then out to the Pickering Creek Trail. We'll take the Station Blvd Trail north to the Eagle Farms Trail east, then turn onto the pleasant Chester Springs Road.
